hero.title: How to Use
hero.subtitle: With TestStudio, crop questions from PDF question banks, organize them in the pool, and build professional exams. This guide walks you through every feature step by step.

s1.title: Overview
s1.desc: TestStudio is an exam preparation platform designed for teachers. Crop questions from your PDF files, organize them in the question pool, and produce professional output on the Layout Desk. It has two main modules: Test Module and Written Module.

interface.title: Interface Overview
interface.body: When you log in, the sidebar appears on the left and the question pool on the right. The sidebar holds your project stats, PDF sources, categories, and action buttons.
interface.imgCaption: Main screen after login — sidebar on the left, question pool on the right

moduleSwitch.title: Module Switcher
moduleSwitch.body: At the top of the sidebar you can switch between the Test Module and the Written Module. The Test Module is for multiple-choice exams; the Written Module is for classic exams with open-ended, true/false, matching, and similar question types.
moduleSwitch.imgAlt: Switching between Test and Written modules
moduleSwitch.imgCaption: Use the module switcher in the sidebar to move between Test and Written

tip.label: Tip:
tip.body: Questions in each module are kept separate. Questions in the Test Module aren't lost when you switch to the Written Module.

s2.title: PDF Cropping
s2.desc: Crop questions from your PDFs by selecting them with the mouse. With smart boundary detection, AI-powered answer recognition, and multi-PDF support, you can move questions into the pool quickly.

upload.title: 2.1 Uploading PDFs
upload.body: Click the "Smart PDF Crop" button in the sidebar. In the dialog that opens, drag and drop your PDF files or use the file picker. You can upload multiple PDFs at once — each one opens in its own tab.
upload.imgCaption: Drag and drop PDFs or upload them with the file picker

navZoom.title: 2.2 Page Navigation and Zoom
navZoom.body: Move between pages using the page navigation on the left panel. Use the zoom slider to enlarge or shrink the PDF.
navZoom.imgCaption: Page navigation and zoom controls in the left panel

crop.title: 2.3 Cropping a Question
crop.body: Select a question area by dragging the mouse on the PDF. You can resize the selection box from its corners. When you make a selection, a toolbar appears:
items: Confirm (✓): Crop the question and add it to the pool
crop.imgCaption: Select the question area with the mouse, mark the answer, and confirm

magnet.title: 2.4 Magnetic Detection
magnet.body: When you turn on the Magnet feature, the selection box automatically snaps to question boundaries. This makes cropping much faster and more precise. Toggle the magnet in the left panel.
magnet.imgCaption: With the magnet on, the selection box snaps to question boundaries

aiAnswer.title: 2.5 AI Answer Recognition
aiAnswer.body: When AI Answer is on, the correct answer of the cropped question is detected automatically by AI. This is a huge time-saver, especially on PDFs that include an answer key.
aiAnswer.imgCaption: AI detects the correct answer of the cropped question automatically

category.title: 2.6 Assigning a Category
category.body: By picking a category in the Category section of the left panel, every question you crop is assigned to it automatically. To create a new category, use the Categories section of the sidebar.
category.imgCaption: Pick the active category while cropping — new questions land in it

tip.label: Tip:
tip.body: You can open multiple PDFs as tabs and switch between them quickly. Each tab keeps its own page and zoom position.

s3.title: Question Pool
s3.desc: All cropped questions land in the question pool. From here you can reorder questions, edit answers, sort by category, and create test groups.

dragDrop.title: 3.1 Drag-and-Drop Reordering
dragDrop.body: Drag the handle (⋮⋮) on a question card to change its order. The Layout Desk lays questions out in this order.
dragDrop.imgCaption: Drag the handle to adjust the question order

answerEdit.title: 3.2 Editing Answers
answerEdit.body: Each question card shows the correct answer at the bottom. Click on it to change the answer. You can pick A, B, C, D, or E, or type a custom answer.
answerEdit.imgCaption: Click the answer field to change the correct answer

categories.title: 3.3 Categories and Colors
categories.body: Add new categories and assign colors in the Categories section of the sidebar. Each question card shows its category as a tag. You can filter and group questions by category.
categories.imgCaption: Use categories to organize questions by lesson or topic

grouping.title: 3.4 Grouping Views
grouping.body: Use the grouping options in the pool toolbar to view questions different ways:
items: By category: Each category is grouped under its own heading
By PDF source: Questions are grouped by the PDF they were cropped from
grouping.imgAlt: Grouping questions by category or PDF source
grouping.imgCaption: Grouping views let you look at your questions from different angles

split.title: 3.5 Splitting the Test (Groups)
split.body: Use the "Split Test" button to split the question pool into multiple groups. You can give each group its own heading and restart numbering. This is ideal for creating different exam variants (A/B) from the same pool.
split.imgCaption: Use Split Test to create A/B groups or distinct sections

multiSelect.title: 3.6 Multi-Select
multiSelect.body: To select multiple questions at once:
items: Ctrl + Click: Add or remove individual questions
Shift + Click: Select a range of questions
multiSelect.outro: On selected questions you can bulk-delete, move, or change category.
multiSelect.imgCaption: Use Ctrl+Click for individual picks, Shift+Click for a range

preview.title: 3.7 Question Preview
preview.body: Double-click a question card, or click the preview button, to see the question at full size. From the preview window you can inspect and edit the question in detail.
preview.imgCaption: Double-click a question to open the full-size preview

tip.label: Tip:
tip.body: For every reorder and edit operation, <kbd class="ln-guide-kbd">Ctrl+Z</kbd> undoes the action and <kbd class="ln-guide-kbd">Ctrl+Y</kbd> redoes it.

s4.title: Layout Desk
s4.desc: The Layout Desk is where you turn your questions into a professional exam. Use page settings, header/footer, templates, and color themes to get the exact output you want.

open.title: 4.1 Opening the Layout Desk
open.body: Click "Layout & Export Desk" in the sidebar to open the Layout Desk. The button becomes active as soon as you have at least one question.
open.imgCaption: Layout Desk — settings on the left, preview in the middle, export on the right

docType.title: 4.2 Document Type
docType.body: Pick one of the document type options in the top bar:
items: Lecture Notes: Lays questions out in a notes format
Written: Written-exam layout (for questions from the Written Module)
docType.imgCaption: Pick Worksheet Test, Lecture Notes, Mock Exam, or Written in the top bar

pageSettings.title: 4.3 Page Settings
pageSettings.body: Configure the page from the left panel:
items: Paper size: A4, A5, Letter, and more
pageSettings.imgCaption: Paper size, orientation, columns, and margin settings

spacing.title: 4.4 Question Spacing
spacing.body: Adjust the gap between questions with the question spacing slider. The preview updates instantly, so you can see how many questions fit on a page in real time.
spacing.imgCaption: Move the slider to adjust the spacing between questions

headerFooter.title: 4.5 Header and Footer
headerFooter.body: Customize the top of your exam sheet — school name, exam name, student info fields, academic year, and more. The footer adds the page number automatically.
headerFooter.imgCaption: Edit the school name, exam title, and student info fields

templates.title: 4.6 Templates
templates.body: Pick one of the Classic, Modern, or Minimal templates in the right panel. Each template uses a different header layout, line style, and typography.
templates.imgCaption: Classic, Modern, and Minimal template options

colors.title: 4.7 Color Themes
colors.body: Pick the theme color of your exam from the color palette in the right panel. The chosen color is applied to headings, lines, and highlight areas.
colors.imgCaption: Pick the theme color of your exam from the color palette

watermark.title: 4.8 Watermark
watermark.body: You can add a transparent watermark to the background of the page. This is useful for preventing copies of the exam sheet or for displaying your school logo.
watermark.imgCaption: Add a school logo or text watermark to the background

tip.label: Tip:
tip.body: All changes on the Layout Desk appear instantly in the preview. Watch the page count and question placement to fine-tune your output.

s5.title: Written Module
s5.desc: The Written Module is designed for classic written exams. It supports open-ended questions, true/false, matching, fill-in-the-blank, and more.

switch.title: 5.1 Switching Modules
switch.body: Click the "Written Module" tab in the module switcher in the sidebar. The pool switches to written questions and different question type options appear.
switch.imgCaption: Switch to the Written Module from the module switcher in the sidebar

types.title: 5.2 Question Types
types.body: In the Written Module you can create the following question types:
items: Open-ended: Free-response questions where students write their answers
types.imgCaption: Mix different question types to create rich written exams

scoring.title: 5.3 Scoring
scoring.body: You can assign separate points to each question. The total score is calculated automatically and shown in the stats panel in the sidebar. On the Layout Desk, the point value appears next to each question.
scoring.imgCaption: Assign points to each question — the total is calculated automatically

edit.title: 5.4 Editing Written Questions
edit.body: You can crop written questions from a PDF or create them by hand. Each question type has its own editor. You can change the order of questions by drag and drop.
edit.imgCaption: Each question type has its own dedicated editor

tip.label: Note:
tip.body: Questions in the Written Module are placed automatically in the written exam layout when you pick the "Written" document type on the Layout Desk.

s6.title: Export
s6.desc: You can download your Layout Desk output in three different formats. Use the export buttons in the right panel.

pdf.title: 6.1 Download PDF
pdf.body: Use Download PDF to download your exam as a high-quality PDF. You get a print-ready, vector output. Watermarks, headers, and all formatting are reflected in the PDF exactly.
pdf.imgCaption: Use Download PDF to get a print-ready output

word.title: 6.2 Download Word
word.body: Use Download Word to download your exam as a .docx file. This format is ideal if you want to keep editing in Word later.
word.imgCaption: Use Download Word to get an editable .docx output

pptx.title: 6.3 Download PowerPoint
pptx.body: Use Download PPTX to download your exam as a PowerPoint presentation. This format is great for showing questions on a smartboard or projector.
pptx.imgCaption: Use Download PPTX to get a presentation-ready output

tip.label: Note:
tip.body: Export may take a few seconds depending on the number of questions. Don't close the page until the download is complete.

s7.title: Saving & Shortcuts
s7.desc: Use auto-save, draft files, and keyboard shortcuts to keep your work safe.

autosave.title: 7.1 Auto-Save
autosave.body: Changes in the question pool are saved automatically to your browser storage (localStorage). Your questions don't disappear when you refresh the page or close the browser.

draft.title: 7.2 Draft File
draft.body: Use the save (💾) button in the pool to download your questions as a draft file to your computer. Use the load (📂) button to restore a previously saved draft. This is ideal for switching between different projects.
draft.imgAlt: Saving and loading a draft file
draft.imgCaption: Manage your projects with the save and load buttons

shortcuts.title: 7.3 Keyboard Shortcuts
shortcuts.body: Use the following shortcuts to speed up your workflow:

tip.label: Tip:
tip.body: We recommend saving your draft file regularly. If browser storage is cleared, the auto-save data may be lost — but your draft file stays safe.

cta.title: Ready?
cta.subtitle: Head to the app and start building your first exam.
